title: What the band earned compared with ordinary jobs
summary: At $66 a week they earned double the Savoy's pay and triple a laborer's, plus hundred dollars doubling in theatres.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Well, these guys look very high-class. In New York you were playing the Cotton Club.
Yeah. You see...
You were playing really high-class places. How much were you making a week?
Sixty-six dollars and sixty-six cents.
Wow. And everybody else who was working regular jobs was making like $15-$20 a week, right?
Well, the Savoy was paying thirty-three dollars and thirty-three cents...
No, I mean ordinary laborers.
Oh yeah, right.
Somebody working on a job was getting like $25 or $30 a week.

Right. Yeah, we were making big money. We were making double the money we made at the Savoy. We were doubling the scale at the Savoy. See, they had a way of going downtown, and by playing so long they could get a scale okay. Because the Savoy did it...
But that's what we're trying to prove, Foots. We're trying to prove what you were making in comparison to what your average person working a regular job was making.
Oh, right. Yes.
Thomas (3) - 20
So that person who working an average job, working in the laundry or working in a restaurant, would make like $20 or $25 a week.
Right.
So if you were making $66 a week, you were making twice.
Yeah, we were making big money. Then when we got to the part where we started doubling in the theatres...
Double what?
[END OF TAPE 5, SIDE A]
We used to double and play the theatres.
Oh, you mean two jobs.

Yeah. And we would get back to the Cotton Club at about 10:30 or 11 o'clock. But they'd have a band to play before we got there, and the thing we had to do was get back to play the show. But we made a hundred dollars a week, plus our salary at the Cotton Club...
You'd get $100 for the theatre.
The theatre...
And you made $66 at the Cotton Club.
